contour.before: Hard-edged zigzag bands and straight spotlight polygons.
contour.after: Soft irregular painted rock strata with no hard overlay in the cave backdrop.

material.before: Flat wall and floor color blocks.
material.after: Brush-modeled limestone depth and distinct stone planes, coherent with the work slab.

palette.after: The same cool cave family with a warmer floor and restrained mica tones. Bright stations stay distinguishable.

light.after: Light is painted into the stone. No separate cave beams or brighter competing source.

perspective.before: Schematic theatre-like walls behind the fixed camera.
perspective.after: Overhead strata and a continuous back-to-front floor, with the original fixed world geometry.

scale.before: Wall spans the fixed 1280 by 720 playfield.
scale.after: Same field and aspect. Native 1664 by 936 crop exceeds the fixed field without enlargement.

contact.before: Station objects and existing actors had no distinct floor plane.
contact.after: A painted floor supports the station row. The imp's elevated action pose and some pre-existing prop/actor overlap remain separate contact work.

occlusion.before: Work slab hides room props through the task guard.
occlusion.after: The same guard and props keep exact ownership. The original curtain and foreground play over the painted cave. No duplicate room items are baked in.

readability.before: Striping and beams cross the figures and invitation.
readability.after: Quiet background improves figure/ground separation. The shared invitation ring and wide viewport side fill remain separately scoped.

action_state.before: Overview, River, Fossil, Pan, Geode and staged result share flat cave geometry.
action_state.after: The plate is stable across all these states. Activity states, foreground visibility, casts, and result framing retain their existing behavior.
